get.description: Search for available flights with optional parameters to filter a search. Results are ordered by route distance (the great-circle distance between the two airports, shortest first; a flight whose airport has no coordinates (unset, or 0/0) comes last), then departure airport, then arrival airport, then flight id, so a route's flights are always adjacent. A page holds at most limit flights (250 at most). When more results follow, the X-SmartCARS-Next-Cursor header carries a cursor: repeat the same request with it as cursor to get the next page. The totals headers count every matching flight, across all pages. A client that ignores the headers gets the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of flights on the page

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The X-SmartCARS-Next-Cursor value of the previous page, to get the page after it. Opaque; it does not expire. Flights added or hidden between pages are neither skipped nor repeated among the remaining results. A change to an airport's coordinates between two page requests can move that route's flights. The other parameters are repeated unchanged.

parameters.name: departureAirport
parameters.description: The ICAO code for the departure airport

parameters.name: arrivalAirport
parameters.description: The ICAO code for the arrival airport

parameters.name: aircraft
parameters.description: The ID of an aircraft; only flights a subfleet containing it can fly are returned, none for an unknown ID. A non-numeric value is ignored

parameters.name: callsign
parameters.description: A callsign pattern to search for (does not have to be exact)

200.description: 200 - Return a page of the available flights

X-SmartCARS-Next-Cursor.description: Present when more results follow; send it back as cursor to get the next page. Absent on the last page.

X-SmartCARS-Total-Flights.description: The number of flights matching the search, across all pages.

X-SmartCARS-Total-Routes.description: The number of distinct departure and arrival airport pairs among the matching flights.

400.description: 400 - Invalid type, or a malformed cursor (message Invalid cursor)

post.description: Search for flights across three dimensions: any of several departure airports, optionally any of several arrival airports, and optionally any of several aircraft. Results are ordered by route distance (the great-circle distance between the two airports, shortest first; a flight whose airport has no coordinates (unset, or 0/0) comes last), then departure airport, then arrival airport, then flight id, so a route's flights are always adjacent. A page holds at most limit flights (250 at most). Without perArrivalLimit the search is paged: when more results follow, the X-SmartCARS-Next-Cursor header carries a cursor, sent back as cursor with the rest of the body unchanged to get the next page, and the totals headers count every matching flight across all pages. A client that ignores the headers gets the first page. When perArrivalLimit is given, at most that many flights are kept per arrival airport, in the same order, before the overall limit is applied; that answer is not paged, carries none of the three headers and ignores cursor. When the only-flights-from-current-airport setting is on, the pilot's current airport is used as the only departure, whatever the request says.

departureAirports.description: The ICAO codes of the possible departure airports; unknown codes are ignored

arrivalAirports.description: The ICAO codes of the possible arrival airports; unknown codes are ignored. When omitted or empty, every arrival is searched

aircraft.description: The ids of the aircraft; only flights whose subfleets contain one of them are returned. When omitted or empty, no aircraft filter applies

limit.description: The maximum number of flights on the page

perArrivalLimit.description: The maximum number of flights to keep per arrival airport, taken in route distance order before limit is applied. Turns paging off

cursor.description: The X-SmartCARS-Next-Cursor value of the previous page, to get the page after it. Opaque; it does not expire. Flights added or hidden between pages are neither skipped nor repeated among the remaining results. A change to an airport's coordinates between two page requests can move that route's flights. Ignored when perArrivalLimit is given

200.description: 200 - Return a page of the available flights

X-SmartCARS-Next-Cursor.description: Present when more results follow; send it back as cursor to get the next page. Absent on the last page and when perArrivalLimit is given.

X-SmartCARS-Total-Flights.description: The number of flights matching the search, across all pages. Absent when perArrivalLimit is given.

X-SmartCARS-Total-Routes.description: The number of distinct departure and arrival airport pairs among the matching flights. Absent when perArrivalLimit is given.

400.description: 400 - Missing departureAirports, or a malformed cursor (message Invalid cursor)

post.description: Cancel an ongoing flight. The unfiled PIREP is cancelled. With the `smartcars.cancel_mode` setting at `delete` it is then deleted together with its ACARS positions, logs and flight analyses, and a SimBrief OFP stays attached to the booked flight; at `cancel` (the default) it stays as a cancelled PIREP. Only the calling pilot's own PIREP is touched; a PIREP that is unknown, already cancelled or deleted, or owned by another pilot answers 200 as well, so the call can be repeated safely. In `delete` mode, a PIREP left in the cancelled state by an earlier call that failed part way is deleted on the next call.

post.description: Record a diversion on an ongoing flight using phpVMS's own diversion handling. The airport is stored in the PIREP's "diversion-airport" field and the PIREP status becomes DV; phpVMS then moves the aircraft and pilot to that airport when the PIREP is filed. A second call replaces the airport. Sending the booked arrival airport removes the diversion again and leaves the status as is; the next /flights/update sets it from the flight phase. While a diversion is recorded, /flights/update keeps the DV status during takeoff, climb, enroute, approach and landing. Only available when the phpVMS "pireps.handle_diversion" setting is on.

post.description: Store flight log lines while the flight is in progress, before it is filed. Each line becomes a phpVMS ACARS log row (type LOG) of the PIREP, shown in the flight log on the PIREP page and in the admin, with the line's message (cut to 255 characters) and its timestamp as the row's time. The row ID is derived from the PIREP ID and the line's index, so the request is idempotent: a line sent again with an index already stored is ignored and the first stored text and time stay. At /flights/complete, a flightData item whose eventId matches an index already stored is not stored a second time; the other items are stored as before. A batch is checked as a whole: one invalid entry refuses the whole request and stores nothing. Expect a client to retry on any status other than those listed (a 500, for example): it sends the same lines again later.

bidID.description: The booking of the flight; accepted but not used

timestamp.description: The line's UTC time, the flightData item's eventTimestamp (e.g. 2026-11-06 14:05:00z)

simTime.description: Optional. The simulator's clock when the line was written; zulu is stored as the row's sim time (acars.sim_time, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS), local is accepted and not stored. A zulu value not in the YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS form, or not a real date, is ignored

Where the aircraft was when the line was written, stored as the row's lat, lon and altitude_msl when all three are finite numbers and latitude and longitude are in range; otherwise the row keeps phpVMS's default position (0, 0, 0) and the line is still stored. The row's altitude_agl is not filled

post.summary: Nudge from the smartCARS backend to run the module auto-update
post.description: Sent by the smartCARS backend when a release of the module is published on GitHub, and once a day as a catch-up. The request is signed with a key only the smartCARS backend holds and verified against the public keys bundled in the module (Support/NudgeKeys.php); there is nothing to configure on the community's side. The body never decides what is installed: the queued update job asks GitHub for the latest published release (drafts and prereleases excluded) and installs that release's commit. Does nothing while the auto-update setting is off. Not called by the smartCARS app.

post.description: Store the smartCARS analyses of a finished flight (landing, flight score, takeoff, trails and debrief), replacing any earlier upload for the same PIREP. Only the calling pilot's own PIREPs are accepted. The payloads are stored as JSON in the sc_flight_analyses table; each part is stored exactly as sent (taken from the raw request body, so empty strings and empty objects survive) and returned the same way by /pireps/analyses/search; the touchdown rate, landing grade and blended flight score are also copied into their own columns. Cancelling a flight deletes its row. A signedLandingAnalysis or signedTakeoffAnalysis that passes every check (among others: a valid signature against the keys bundled in the module, a JSON object payload of version 1 for this kind and PIREP, the uploading pilot when the payload names an airline pilot, and an analysis that is an object) is stored in place of the unsigned landingAnalysis or takeoffAnalysis and marks it verified; the unsigned copy sent beside it is neither compared nor stored. A signed part that is missing, malformed or fails a check never fails the upload: the unsigned analysis is stored as sent and it is not verified; the reason is logged for a part that was sent (a missing part logs nothing). A well-formed signed part is stored as sent whether or not it verified.

alternateAirport.description: The alternate airport published on the flight, null when it has none

distance.description: The distance in nautical miles, whatever the VA's display unit

daysOfWeek.description: The days the flight operates, Monday first; empty when the flight has no days set

extensions.description: The flight's custom field values (phpVMS flight fields)

rankLevel.description: Deprecated, still sent: the 0-based position of the pilot's rank among the ranks ordered by hours. The aircraft's restriction says which aircraft the pilot may fly.

extensions.description: The pilot's custom field values (phpVMS user fields), private fields included; inactive and internal fields are left out

LandingAnalysis.description: smartCARS landing analysis (LandingAnalysisSchema in the app). Stored as JSON; only the fields named here are read by this API, the rest is passed through.

distanceFromThresholdM.description: Signed; negative = short of the (displaced) threshold

FlightScore.description: smartCARS flight score (FlightScoreSchema in the app): rule deductions plus the landing blend.

current.description: initial minus every deduction, at least 0

landingPct.description: Landing performance out of 100; null before the landing is scored

blended.description: 60% flight score + 40% landing performance. Stored in sc_flight_analyses.flight_score

ApproachSample.description: One sample of the approach or takeoff trail (ApproachSampleSchema in the app).

TakeoffAnalysis.description: smartCARS takeoff analysis (TakeoffAnalysisSchema in the app). Stored as JSON and passed through.

FlightDebrief.description: smartCARS flight debrief record (FlightDebriefRecordSchema in the app). Stored as JSON and passed through.
